annotations.title: Calculate a material quantity (how much, how many)

description: Computes the result of one calculator, identified by its slug, from the input values given: the amount of material a job needs, such as the bags of concrete for a slab or the sheets of drywall for a room, counted in bags, sheets, studs, tiles, litres, gallons, cubic yards or m³. Returns it in metric and US units with the inputs used, sources, a citation and the page link. No prices.

detail.description: full (the default): the whole answer. summary: the result lines, the citation line and the page only — fewer tokens to read.

explain.description: true adds the working: the inputs as the calculator received them, every intermediate figure its own compute reports with its unit, the range check and the unit restatement, ending on the same figures. The answer's figures are identical either way.

inputUnits.description: Send "base" to pass bare numbers on dimensioned inputs in base units (m, m², L, kg …), as the published test vectors are written. Without it a length, area or volume must carry its unit.

inputs.description: The calculator's input values, by input id (an unknown id is refused with the accepted ids). A length, area, volume or other measured input takes "12 ft", "3.5 m", "8' 3 1/2\"" or {"value": 12, "unit": "ft"}; a count or percentage takes a number; a select takes one of its option values. Inputs left out take the value the calculator's page opens on.

market.description: Optional. A market whose own opening choice some inputs take (a UK reader's code, an IEC motor), and whose currency symbol prints the caller's own money figures.

slug.description: The calculator's slug, such as concrete-calculator.

system.description: The unit system inputs left out open in, and the one the page link opens in. The answer comes in both.

name: calculate

json.description: The calculator's static API document, with its test vectors.

lastVerified.description: The date the calculator's sources were last checked.

version.description: The calculator's own version; a result names the calculator that produced it.

explain.description: Only when explain is true. Each figure is the calculator's own; no step is a formula written for the engine.

coverage.description: result-only: the calculator reports no figures between its inputs and its result.

final.description: The figures the answer returns, copied from it.

limits.description: What the trace does not show, and why.

movedBy.description: Input ids whose change moved this figure, measured by running compute again.

unit.description: The calculator's own (base) unit for the value.

inputs.description: Every input the calculation ran on, and where each came from.

open.description: Opens the page on these inputs.

canonical.description: The figure in the calculator's own unit, before the display adapter: what its test vectors pin.

isComparison.description: The figure is set against a limit. It is not an approval.

anyOf.description: The headline exactly as the page prints it.
